Article 8
(1) The Regent integrates policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women into the Regional development planning.
(2) The integration of programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be incorporated into planning and budget documents which include:
a. regional long-term development plan; b. regional medium-term development plan; c. strategic plan of Regional Apparatus;
d. work plan of Regional Government; and e. work plan and budget of Regional Apparatus. (3) The Regional Apparatus handling the field of Women shall facilitate the integration of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women into the preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (2).
(4) In carrying out activities as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Apparatus handling the field of Women shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that have direct relevance to the field of Women.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 5
Letter a What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causing death.
Letter b What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Letter c What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
Letter d What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other parties;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after women as wives as appropriate, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other parties
c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting work
Letter e What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter f What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits whether material or immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 9
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Letter a What is meant by policy analysis is applied social research that is systematically compiled in order to determine the substance of the policy so that information regarding the problems answered by the policy and problems that may arise as a result of the implementation of the policy can be clearly known. Letter b What is meant by advocacy is social, political and cultural action carried out in a planned, structured manner, and conducted collectively, involving various tactics including lobbying, campaigns, establishing coalitions, applying pressure through mass actions, as well as research used to change policy.
Letter c What is meant by coordination is activities carried out by various parties of equal standing to mutually provide information and jointly arrange or agree upon something, while communication is a process in which a person or several persons, groups, organizations, and society create and use information in order to connect with the environment and other people.
Letter d What is meant by socialization is the process of instilling or transferring habits or values and rules from one generation to another generation within a group or society. Letter e What is meant by education is a learning process carried out both formally and informally that aims to educate, provide knowledge and develop human potential and realize that learning process in a better way.
Letter f What is meant by training is a process where people achieve certain abilities to help achieve organizational goals and is part of education concerning the learning process to acquire and improve skills outside the prevailing education system in a relatively short time with methods that prioritize practice over theory.
Letter g What is meant by facilitation is a conscious process to assist a community group so that they can successfully carry out their tasks while maintaining the existence of that group.

2.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, there is clear institutionalisation of integrating women’s protection into government planning and strengthening gender institutions: Pasal 8(1)-(4) requires the Bupati to “mengintegrasikan kebijakan, program, dan kegiatan Perlindungan Perempuan ke dalam perencanaan pembangunan Daerah” and embeds it in formal planning/budget documents (RPJPD, RPJMD, Renstra OPD, RKPD, RKA OPD). Pasal 10(1) huruf c explicitly mandates “penguatan kapasitas kelembagaan Gender.” These provisions were present in the retrieved English candidates ([2.4-13] and [2.4-15]). The judge incorrectly required an explicit mention of ‘gender mainstreaming’ or a specific working group; the indicator can be satisfied by formal integration into planning/budget systems and institutional capacity strengthening, which the regulation provides.

4.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text includes primary-prevention education/information elements: Pasal 13(b) mandates the local government to “melakukan sosialisasi terhadap hak Perempuan” and Pasal 21(1)(a) allows community participation via “pemberian penyuluhan mengenai hak Perempuan.” The Penjelasan Umum also frames objectives including “Memberikan keadilan dan kesetaraan gender.” These are directly about disseminating information/education on women’s rights (and linked to gender equality). The retrieved English candidates contained these points ([4.2-20], [4.2-30], [4.2-46]), so the judge’s ‘Yes’ is supported. Thus the golden label ‘No’ likely is incorrect.
